dedupe_keys.name: broadcasting in the national early warning and resilience strategy itu session slides asia media summit july 2025

description: These 63 slides, presented by the ITU at the 20th Asia Media Summit on 21 July 2025, set out the role of broadcasting in disseminating early warnings across the Asia-Pacific region within the Early Warnings for All initiative and multi-hazard early warning systems. The opening slides give the economic case: early warnings return more than tenfold on investment; the World Bank estimate of avoided annual losses of $35 billion from universal access; a WFP-led Emergency Telecommunications Cluster study finding a return of almost three dollars per dollar invested; and the Global Commission on Adaptation finding that 24 hours of warning cuts damage by 30 percent. Later slides show how broadcasters and telecoms increase resilience by sharing infrastructure, including news gathering by satellite and microwave, One-Seg mobile TV in Japan, FM in phones in Europe, and short wave when local infrastructure is damaged. Producer: ITU, July 2025. Coverage: Asia-Pacific. Access: free PDF; slides 1 to 5 and 21 to 23 were read. Licence and cost: free; licence not stated. Caveats: slides quote figures from other studies without full citation. Simulation uses: the benefit and channel descriptions inform emergency-response and adaptation models that include broadcast warning channels. Related record: the ITU Connect2Recover resilience study (case_study-itu-connect2recover-national-ict-infrastructure-resilience-asia-pacifi).
